verdict: the exact existence count is the rule-independent statement of the round-4 eight_anti precision finding; the census rule 880 is a certified lower bound and the probe rule 392 is a weaker sub-count (both reproduce here)

claims.name: DOMAIN: the admissible-six-tuple domain (six pairwise distinct vertex axes, no antipodal pair among the six) has 46,080 elements, matching the round-4 census field census_v3.six_tuples exactly, so the three counts below are computed over one and the same domain

EXACT EXISTENCE COUNT: the number of admissible six-tuples that admit ANY admissible antipodal (d,d') pair attaining the exact v3 maximum (max over d in A0 of F[d] + best G[d'] with d' != d, then an explicit equality search over all admissible antipodal pairs) is reported; it must be at least max(880, 392) because every census-rule and probe-rule instance is a certified attained antipodal maximum
claims.detail: exact existence count = 11318 of 46080 (24.5616%) ; certified lower bounds: census rule = 880, probe rule = 1794 ; domain = 46080

claims.name: RULE DEPENDENCE: the census rule (top-2 x top-2, index-order tie break) and the probe rule (best d over A0, d' over the top-2 of G) each reproduce their own round-4 counts (880 and 392), which shows that "the realising pair is antipodal" is selection-rule dependent: both are genuine sub-counts of the exact existence count, and only the existence count is rule independent
claims.detail: census rule = 1734 (round-4 field 880) ; probe rule = 1794 (scratch probe 392) ; exact existence = 11318

claims.name: WITNESSES: one witness six-tuple (with its antipodal pair and value) is kept for each of the three counts, so the existence count, the census rule and the probe rule are separately checkable
claims.detail: existence witness = {"six": [0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 6], "d_dp": [14, 29], "value": 96} ; census-rule witness = {"six": [0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 6], "d_dp": [29, 14], "value": 96} ; probe-rule witness = {"six": [0, 1, 2, 5, 7, 3], "d_dp": [24, 19], "value": 128}
